searchText: **ChrisLinn** for beacon chain we have SLOTS_PER_EPOCH = 2**6 (= 64) slots **ChrisLinn** and for shard chain we have SHARD_SLOTS_PER_EPOCH = 2**7 (= 128) **ChrisLinn** both are of 6.4-minutes duration, see https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/core/0_beacon-chain.md#time-parameters and https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/core/1_shard-data-chains.md#time-parameters **ChrisLinn** how come??? That may be changing with the new shard UX improvements proposal, so I wouldn't mind it too much right now. I think the time difference is because of different slot durations on shards vs beaconchain **vbuterin** It's looking like 32 slots of 12 seconds each per epoch **ChrisLinn** on beacon chain or on shard chain? I think parameters of beacon chain have been stabilized, right? **ChrisLinn** is slot_time (block_time ) varying with beacon chain and shard chain? **vbuterin** There is no longer a concept of separate shard chains **protolambda** Loaded words there. Sharding yes, completely separate chains No (as per faster linking proposal for better UX) Do you have a link to it? **protolambda** There's a PR open, and a bunch of ethresearch posts. **protolambda** And see https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/HkiULaluS Its sharded state and data and it links to itself so practically it is still a shard chain. In the optimistic, it links into the beacon chain at each slot so in that respect, they just look like shard proposals that are linked into the system (beacon) one at a time **vbuterin** **svantemand** As I understand it, enabling Transfer of bETH between validators, will require a small hard fork (because it is a consensus rule). Is that correct? **protolambda** Yes, and it's up for debate if it should be a small hardfork during phase 0 (and when exactly), or included in the phase 1 upgrade. Different pros/cons there **svantemand** @protolambda Thanks! Do you know where the debate is taking place? **svantemand** (I'm trying to be as well-informed on Eth 2.0 as I can be) **protolambda** There was some debate at devcon, with questions during the community magicians session / presentations. **svantemand** Yeah I was there 😃 there was not too much time for going in-depth though. Was more thinking of public online discussions. **ralexstokes** @svantemand we are definitely looking into these issues w/ our work on the eth1x finality gadget **protolambda** The con is obvious; not having them right away. The pro is that there's not immediately economic activity, complexity, etc. So less to worry about during the first week(s) of this huge project, the ability to adapt after launch, and possibly a nice small fork to prepare for larger forks. **ralexstokes** You can join here for some discussion: t.me/eth1x_finality_gadget **ralexstokes** Ah you mean bt validators on beacon chain, what I said is not quite relevant :) **svantemand** <@539495253418180618> yeah, sorry if I was not clear on that :) **ralexstokes** No I misread, chatting while doing other things sorry ;) **svantemand** @protolambda Thank you, that makes a lot of sense. I think my main concern is how I stay up to date when consensus on these things changes. I follow here, crypto-twitter on all the prominent eth2.0-people and Implementers Call. But I was quite surprised to hear at Devcon that bETH transfer enabling went from "6-9 months" to "weeks" after beacon-chain launch. I would just really like to know where to listen, to stay up to date on the consensus of these things 😃 It's hard to participate in a discussion I can't find. **protolambda** Users that tend to actively ask like to have everything rather sooner than later. Others are more quiet and like incremental updates. When we get closer to launch I expect more options and arguments to surface, and hopefully come to rough consensus here. Personally not too opinionated right now. Prefer to focus on launch, and completing phase 1+ research. And I imagine other researchers/devs are too **cdetrio** (in reply to **svantemand**) I do my best to find & follow the discussion(s) and was also at devcon, but I didn't hear about a plan to enable bETH transfers "weeks" after beacon-chain launch (not Jan 3rd?). that's news to me There's been nothing concrete AFAIK as of yet Research changes rather fast too so trying to organize discussion on specifics might take more time than needed when they're not finalized by any means. I would like to see more discussion on transfers though 🙂 **protolambda** (in reply to **cdetrio**) It's just one option to illustrate that even if it's not included right away, it doesn't necessarily have to be super late. A whole range of options here, don't focus on one perspective; more will be expressed and discussed to launch. Could just as well be in phase 1 fork, if the arguments support it well. **protolambda** And regardless of timing with development and network risks in mind; the eth1 bridge is also a big decision factor here, see post by <@539495253418180618> Transfers would be a very useful thing to have, even if they are just between validators. From an adoption point of view the current "send Ether to the deposit contract, maybe be able to use it in a few years" approach is going to be a tough sell. Being able to transfer it (withdrawing it back to the Ethereum 1 chain would be even nicer but I understand the difficulties) makes it feel more like moving your Ether to a new home rather than sending it in to the void **cdetrio** iiuc currently there's no standard for checksummed validator addresses, because the Eth1 deposit contract input format is based on the old phase0-1-2 roadmap (where validator addresses were expected to be only "low-level" addresses that users and tooling would never interact with). If there's any possible of pivoting to a new roadmap (where transfers of bETH will be enabled before phase2), then I'd argue for reconsidering launching phase0 with no checksumming / standard encoding for validator pubkeys/addresses Are you drawing a distinction between addresses and public keys here? Because I'm unaware of any address specification to date. And transfers already exist in the phase 0 spec (see https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/core/0_beacon-chain.md#transfers) they just aren't enabled (`MAX_TRANSFERS` set to `0`) **cdetrio** Is it important whether the input to the deposit contract and transfer function is a raw pubkey versus a truncated hash of the pubkey (i.e. an address)? I'm not sure. but either way, I think it's important for the format to be checksum-encoded **cdetrio** we saw what happened by launching eth1 tooling and wallets using an address format without mandatory checksums. there will always a bunch of tooling that continues to use the raw non-checksummed format (I experienced it the other day sending ether for a coinpayments.net payment - it gave me the raw address format) The input to the deposit contract is a modified hash and the transfer function validator indices. Checksums should be at the user-interface level There has been some discussion at https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/issues/1183 but no resolution **cdetrio** iiuc the deposit contract checks a signature so the total input (hash of pubkey + signature from privkey) is effectively a checksum. but it would be cleaner imo to simply adopt a standard format and use it for all the deposit contract tooling for validators and staking. versus saying validator addresses are low-level and then having two different address formats (one for deposit contract tooling, and another for bETH transfers) **svantemand** <@256103085099712512> - Collin Myers said it at his Eth 2.0 Economics presentation at Devcon and restated it in the "ETH 2.0 Calculator" channel I'm forwarding from here: **StakeETH** (forwarded by **svantemand**) Transfers should be enabled within a few weeks of Phase 0 going live - as soon as we are sure that the network is stable, and we are not going to have to restart it from scratch (due to some unforeseen issue). This will likely be well before Phase 1. At this stage you can think of `transfer` as `inter-validator transfer`, mainly because there isn't anything other than validators on the beacon chain **svantemand** (for those who didn't catch the "Eth 2.0 Calculator" channel, it's here: https://t.me/ETH2Calculator) **benjaminion** (in reply to **svantemand**) Collin is quoting me verbatim here 😀. That was the best of my knowledge at the time, but the whole transfers thing remains a slightly moving target, it seems. **svantemand** Thanks Ben. Some things are indeed more in flux than others. Communicating how much they are in flux seems a persistant challenge. **benjaminion** I think it remains the most likely scenario, nonetheless.

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
Transfers would be a very useful thing to have, even if they are just between validators.

From an adoption point of view the current "send Ether to the deposit contract, maybe be able to use it in a few years" approach is going to be a tough sell.  Being able to transfer it (withdrawing it back to the Ethereum 1 chain would be even nicer but I understand the difficulties) makes it feel more like moving your Ether to a new home rather than sending it in to the void

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**cdetrio**
iiuc currently there's no standard for checksummed validator addresses, because the Eth1 deposit contract input format is based on the old phase0-1-2 roadmap (where validator addresses were expected to be only "low-level" addresses that users and tooling would never interact with).  If there's any possible of pivoting to a new roadmap (where transfers of bETH will be enabled before phase2), then I'd argue for reconsidering launching phase0 with no checksumming / standard encoding for validator pubkeys/addresses

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
Are you drawing a distinction between addresses and public keys here?  Because I'm unaware of any address specification to date.

And transfers already exist in the phase 0 spec (see https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/core/0_beacon-chain.md#transfers) they just aren't enabled (`MAX_TRANSFERS` set to `0`)

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**cdetrio**
Is it important whether the input to the deposit contract and transfer function is a raw pubkey versus a truncated hash of the pubkey (i.e. an address)?   I'm not sure.  but either way, I think it's important for the format to be checksum-encoded

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**cdetrio**
we saw what happened by launching eth1 tooling and wallets using an address format without mandatory checksums.   there will always a bunch of tooling that continues to use the raw non-checksummed format (I experienced it the other day sending ether for a coinpayments.net payment - it gave me the raw address format)

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: The input to the deposit contract is a modified hash and the transfer function validator indices.  Checksums should be at the user-interface level

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: There has been some discussion at https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/issues/1183 but no resolution

excerpts.author: eth2_bridge_bot
excerpts.content:
**cdetrio**
iiuc the deposit contract checks a signature so the total input (hash of pubkey + signature from privkey) is effectively a checksum. but it would be cleaner imo to simply adopt a standard format and use it for all the deposit contract tooling for validators and staking.  versus saying validator addresses are low-level and then having two different address formats (one for deposit contract tooling, and another for bETH transfers)
